hook: Two friends look at the same blurry photo. One sees a rat, the other an old man with glasses. Nothing about the light reaching their eyes is different. What differs is what their brains expected, and that is perception at work.

prereq.q: Which step happens in sensation, before perception begins?
options: Receptors change light into neural signals (transduction)
The brain decides what an object is
A memory of the object is formed
Attention picks one conversation to follow
prereq.why: Sensation is detecting the stimulus: receptors transduce energy into neural signals. Interpreting those signals is perception.

prereq.q: Which lobe of the brain first processes visual information?
prereq.why: The occipital lobe, at the back of the brain, holds the primary visual cortex.

figure.caption: Four Gestalt principles: proximity, similarity, closure and figure-ground.

chain.cause: Receptors send signals about lines, edges and colors
chain.effect: bottom-up processing begins to build a picture of the scene

chain.cause: Knowledge, expectations and context join in
chain.effect: top-down processing and perceptual set tilt what we perceive

chain.cause: The brain applies Gestalt grouping and depth cues
chain.effect: we see whole objects, at a distance, in three dimensions
what we do not attend to can go unseen (inattentional and change blindness)

ideas: Bottom-up processing builds a percept from raw features; top-down processing uses knowledge, schemas and expectations (perceptual set). Both run at once.
Selective attention filters input. Important words still break through (the cocktail party effect), but unattended things can be missed (change blindness, inattentional blindness).
Gestalt principles group parts into wholes: proximity, similarity, closure and figure-ground.
Depth comes from binocular cues (retinal disparity, convergence) and monocular cues (relative size, interposition, linear perspective, texture gradient, relative clarity).
Perceptual constancy keeps size, shape and color stable; apparent movement turns still frames into motion.

misconception.wrong: Your eyes work like a camera, so what you see is an exact copy of the world.
misconception.right: Perception is built by the brain. The same image can be seen two ways depending on expectations, context and attention, and things in plain view can be missed entirely.

summary: Perception turns sensations into meaning. It is built bottom-up from features and top-down from knowledge and expectations, filtered by limited attention, organized by Gestalt principles, given depth by binocular and monocular cues, and kept stable by perceptual constancy.
